subject: Anthropic Claude Code runs parallel cloud threads while your laptop is
intro: AI is going vertical. Not just smarter, but domain-native . OpenAI wrapping GPT-6 Astra in 230M legal URLs isn't a product launch, it's a land grab on professional knowledge work. Law today, medicine tomorrow. Meanwhile Anthropic ships Claude Code Projects that keep coding after you close your laptop. The agent doesn't wait for you anymore. That's the real shift. We're watching the same pattern everywhere: models stop being tools and start being colleagues . Slightly cheaper ones.

news.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Astra for law firms with 230M-URL legal search index
news.body: OpenAI just dropped Astra for Law , a version of GPT-6 Astra tuned specifically for legal work. Think of it like giving a brilliant AI assistant a law degree and a library card. Here's what makes it different from just using regular ChatGPT: For you as a builder, the API is coming soon. OpenAI maintains the legal configuration, so you focus on your product, not the plumbing. Access starts through Trusted Access in ChatGPT and Codex, with expanded privacy and governance controls for eligible firms. The people who know the work are shaping the tools.
bullets: A Legal Search Index covering U.S. case law, statutes, regulations, and court rules across 230 million URLs , updated daily
Settings pre-configured for thorough, careful legal analysis and writing
73 plugins total (26 partner-built, 47 community-built) connecting tools lawyers already use
Real firm workflows already built: agreement analysis, M&A due diligence, and IPO prep

news.headline: Anthropic ships Claude Code Projects, running parallel cloud threads while you're offline
news.body: Claude Code just flipped what a "project" means. It used to be a folder with files and one chat. Now it's a single conversation that manages itself . Here's what actually happens: you describe a goal, and Claude figures out how to split it up. It spins up parallel cloud threads , each working on its own branch and copy of your repo, opening pull requests and running tests on its own. The big unlock? Threads keep running after you close your laptop. You can check in from your phone. No babysitting required. One heads-up: running multiple full sessions burns credits fast. Watch your usage. Also, local files and internal networks are not supported yet, cloud only for now. Available in beta for Pro and Max users. Join the waitlist to get in.
bullets: You describe the goal, Claude decides how to split the work
Each thread gets its own repo branch and runs as a full cloud session
Shared memory keeps context flowing between all threads
You can set smarter models for the coordinator, cheaper ones for routine worker threads

news.headline: Open-source browser agent finds flights in 7 seconds for less than half a cent
news.body: Browser Use + Jev is an open-source browser agent that controls Chrome the way a human would, but absurdly faster. It found flights from Zurich to London in 7 seconds and spent just $0.0039 doing it. Here is what makes it fast. Most browser agents take a screenshot, send it to an AI, wait for instructions, repeat. Jev skips screenshots entirely. Instead, it reads the page as structured data, like a numbered list of every button and input on screen, then picks what to do next in one network call. You can clone it, point it at any URL, give it a plain-English goal, and let it run. It works on flights, Wikipedia, hotel searches, and more.
bullets: Every page load produces a fresh numbered element table: buttons, dropdowns, text fields
One AI call picks the action AND the target at the same time
A small, cheap model only activates when typing is needed
Browser calls dropped from 1,092 to 101, a 25% speed improvement
